status.en: 210 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 16% fewer than the week before, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 210 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 16 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen attacked a Plateau community, killing four civilians and later burned a vigilante office while troops arrested two suspects. In Ekiti, Sowore was assaulted by alleged political thugs and accused police of downplaying the incident, while another report says he was abducted. Nigerian troops killed 48 ISWAP fighters and one soldier in battles in Borno and Yobe. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenmenn angrep et samfunn i Plateau, drepte fire sivile og brente senere et vigilante-kontor mens tropper arresterte to mistenkte. I Ekiti ble Sowore angrepet av påståtte politiske gjengmedlemmer, og han anklaget politiet for å bagatellisere hendelsen, mens en annen rapport hevder at han ble bortført. Nigeriske tropper drepte 48 ISWAP-krigere og én soldat i kamper i Borno og Yobe. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
